Promoted from finance director eight months before an IPO process. We worked on presence with the board and on letting a strong team be strong.
+A founder who stopped being the bottleneck.
Forty people, every decision through one inbox. A year later the exec team runs the week and the founder runs the next three years.
yTechnically brilliant, politically invisible. We built a way of being heard in rooms where the loudest voice usually won.
0Leading eleven thousand people through a merger.
Two cultures, one winter. The work was about tempo: what to decide this week, what to refuse to decide, and how to say both out loud.
kNGMqDEXe-chunk-default-0.framercms: Twenty-five minutes, no charge. You tell me what is going on, I tell you how I would approach it, and we both decide whether there is a fit. About half of calls end with a referral to someone better suited.
4How is coaching different from mentoring or therapy?
A mentor gives you their answers. A therapist helps you heal. A coach helps you see how you operate, decide what to change, and practise it under real conditions
with evidence from the people around you.
%How do you measure whether it worked?
We agree two or three observable behaviours at the start and run short 360 pulse surveys at the beginning, midpoint and end. You see the numbers move, or we change the approach.
pSessions run in Marylebone or on video
most clients mix both. Shadowing days happen wherever your work does.
I work with twelve principals at a time and open three places a quarter. If the timing is wrong I will say so on the first call and hold a place where I can.
Can my company pay for this?
about two thirds of engagements are sponsored. I send a one-page summary and a simple agreement, and the sponsor gets a short progress note each quarter. Never session content.
#How do I know which programme fits?
You do not need to. We work that out on the chemistry call; about a third of people end up somewhere other than where they expected.
What if it is not working?
We will both know by the midpoint pulse. If the numbers have not moved we change the approach, and if they still do not, we stop and you are not billed for the remainder.
tYes, through The Leadership Bench. I only take team work where the chief executive is in the room for every session.
Most engagements are sponsored by the company; around a third are paid privately. Either way the conversations are confidential. Sponsors hear themes and progress, never content.

*If the real conversation happens in the corridor, your meeting is theatre.
Most executive teams I meet are polite in the room and honest outside it. The fix is rarely a new agenda. It is a leader who can hear disagreement without punishing it
and who proves that, visibly, three or four times.
New CEOs arrive with a deck. The ones who last arrive with questions.

A plan written before you have met the people who must carry it is a guess with formatting. Spend the first month listening in a structured way, and publish what you heard before you publish what you will do.
Some decisions improve with a week of thought; some rot in a day. Naming which is which, out loud, is one of the most calming things a leader can do for a team under pressure.
The more senior you are, the older your information about yourself.
By the time feedback reaches a chief executive it has been softened four times. Build a small, protected channel
two people, one question, every fortnight
